name: Mystikal
notes: A funk record with a rapper on it, and the model has to be built the way the records were: around a voice the engine does not have. ⛔ **"Sparse sustained melody — the voice is the lead instrument."** That is the sourced claim, and it makes `melody.emptyBarBias` 0.2 — the highest anywhere in this lane, against the parent's 0.06 and crunk's 0.15 — with `densityPerBar` at 2–6 and `timbreHint` `horn_stab`, because what plays in the gaps is horn stabs, organ and rhythm-guitar scratch rather than a lead line. The archetype fills the bar with keyboards; this artist empties it for a shout. ⛔ **The bass is the most independent in this batch.** "Syncopated synth or played bass line in a funk 16th rhythm; 808 for weight only" — so `followRootsProb` drops to 0.4 (the parent is 0.55), `anticipationProb` rises to 0.36, the cell shapes are funk figures rather than root pedals, and the 808's own `slideProb` falls to 0.03 because it is carrying weight, not melody. ⛔ **16th ghost snares and live-feel hats.** The research names ghost snares specifically, so `snare.ghost.prob` is 0.5 — more than double the parent's 0.22 — across four 16th positions, and `quantizeStrength` drops to 0.8 with `velocityVar` at 0.2 to get the live feel. The drum part "answers the vocal's accents", which is what `melody.structure: call_response` and the very high `dropOutBeats.prob` stand in for: stop-time hits under vocal accents, expressed as the arrangement dropping out rather than as a vocal lane. ⚠ **Harmony is a single i7 groove**, so `chords.impliedByRiff` is set and `extensions.seventh` is the highest in this batch; the "occasional i–IV shuffle" is the second family, and IV over dorian is what makes it a shuffle rather than a modulation. Variety comes from a 4–16 beat `chordDurationBeats`, three `harmonicRhythm` values and a wide `voicing.register`, not from progressions these records do not play. ⚠ **Confidence `medium` because the research rates it medium-high** and marks the 92–104 band **[LOW-CONF]** — the vocal-rhythmic model is what is sourced, and a vocal-rhythmic model is exactly the part a MIDI engine cannot hold. Inferred: the key list, every velocity and register bound, the `intervals`/`contour` split, the perc lanes and the exact ghost probability. ⚠ `snareRoll.pitchWalk` is inherited. ⚠ **A register here spanned less than an octave and has been widened.** The 808 places its root with `pitch_class_in_register`, which returns nothing — and therefore writes NO 808 at all — when the window holds no octave of the key it was asked for. An eleven-semitone window misses one pitch class entirely, so the part vanished on every seed that landed in that key. The centre of the authored range is unchanged. ⚠ The bass ceiling came down from 47 to 44 so it stays under a chord part that starts at 45 — `coherence.rs` requires the highest bass note to sit at or below the lowest chord note, and this model overlapped by 3. ⚠ **The 1-bar phrase length was removed** (was [2,4,1], now [2,4]). A one-bar phrase looped four times carries less entropy than a four-bar phrase, and it is the countermelody it strangles hardest: a counter answers *inside* the melody’s phrase, so a one-bar shape leaves it nowhere to go. Every worst offender on `counter.rs` carried it. ⛔ The previous session recorded this exact mistake and it arrived again from the other direction — distinctness is combinatorial in the shape LENGTH, not in the option count.
